svg.title: PureHDF Read Path — Driver & Stream Selection by Use Case
svg.desc: Use-case decision diagram: for each source scenario (local file by path, memory-mapped file, in-memory byte buffer, plain Stream, custom IConcurrentStream, Amazon S3 stream) the H5File.Open overload used, the internal driver selected, the stream contract (IConcurrentStream positionless vs plain Stream cursor vs memory), the underlying IO source and its cost tier, and whether concurrent reads and genuine suspension apply.
svg.text: PureHDF Read Path — Driver & Stream Selection by Use Case
Which H5File.Open overload, which internal driver, and which stream contract applies to each source scenario

Which H5File.Open overload you call to open the file
caller owns the buffer · driver never writes
no async overload — always a sync source

SYNC · never queues to the thread pool

Can multiple threads read from the same opened file at once?
per-op driver · own cursor · shared SafeFileHandle
second driver = own _position · accessor is safe
returns null · shared cursor — concurrent reads race
per-op driver · positionless · no shared cursor
Does ReadAsync actually yield to the caller, or complete synchronously?
a local file is not an asynchronous source
an in-memory buffer is genuinely synchronous
the async path exists for this source
CreateDriver selection rules (H5File.cs — shared by sync and async stream overloads)
→ H5StreamDriver positionless mode (IConcurrentStream constructor). The cursor lives in the driver; the source is never seeked; reads are concurrent.
→ A FileStream is unwrapped to H5FileHandleDriver (positional pread); its own cursor is never used.
Any other Stream → H5StreamDriver cursor mode (Stream constructor): Stream.Seek + Stream.ReadAsync, non-concurrent.

The mode is chosen by which overload is called — there is no auto-detection. A Stream that also implements IConcurrentStream gets cursor mode through the Stream overload; the caller picks positionless by passing it as IConcurrentStream instead.
Pick the column matching your source. The vertical flow is: public API you call → internal driver selected → stream contract used → underlying IO + cost tier → concurrency and suspension behavior.

The only genuinely-suspending sources are IConcurrentStream implementations (e.g. a custom HTTP range source, Amazon S3). Local files, memory-mapped views and in-memory buffers always complete synchronously and return an already-completed ValueTask.

Concurrency is available on every source except one opened through the Stream overload (cursor mode): resolve the object first (single-threaded, file-level cursor), then read in parallel — one driver per operation, each with its own cursor.

Drivers (H5FileHandleDriver, H5StreamDriver, H5MemoryMappedFileDriver, H5MemoryDriver) and ReadAheadWindow are internal — not public API. The public contracts are H5File.Open*, IConcurrentStream and the async read/navigation members.
